questions.q: What does it mean for an HTTP method to be 'idempotent'?
options: It can only be called once per day
It requires authentication, unlike other methods
Calling it once has the same end effect as calling it multiple times
It always returns a 500 status code
questions.explain: Idempotent means repeated identical calls leave the resource in the same end state as a single call — DELETE and PUT are idempotent; POST generally is not.

questions.q: Why is POST /orders considered NOT idempotent, while DELETE /orders/1001 IS idempotent?
options: POST always fails on the second call, while DELETE always succeeds
Calling POST /orders twice creates two separate orders, while calling DELETE /orders/1001 twice ends with the same result (the order gone)
POST and DELETE are actually both idempotent
Idempotency only applies to GET requests
questions.explain: Each POST call creates a brand-new resource (a different end state each time), while repeated DELETE calls on the same resource all end with it gone.

questions.q: What's the key difference between PUT and PATCH?
options: PUT replaces the entire resource (omitted fields may be cleared); PATCH updates only the fields included in the request
PUT and PATCH are exactly the same method with different names
PATCH can only be used on GET requests
PUT is only for creating new resources, never updating
questions.explain: PUT sends a full replacement for the resource; PATCH sends a partial update, leaving unmentioned fields untouched.

questions.q: What does an HTTP status code's first digit tell you?
options: Nothing useful — you must read the full code to know anything
The general category: e.g. 2xx success, 4xx client error, 5xx server error
The exact server that handled the request
How many retries the client has attempted
questions.explain: The first digit groups status codes into categories — 1xx informational, 2xx success, 3xx redirection, 4xx client error, 5xx server error.

questions.q: A request returns 401 Unauthorized. What does that most likely mean?
options: The server crashed while processing an otherwise valid request
The requested resource doesn't exist
Credentials are missing or invalid
The request succeeded but returned no data
questions.explain: 401 Unauthorized specifically signals a problem with authentication — missing or invalid credentials — distinct from 403 Forbidden (valid credentials, not allowed) or 404 Not Found.
